correctness.rationale: Finite-dimensional input fibers make every finite-coordinate truncation finite rank, so each finite-propagation approximation has norm at least its essential norm on every coordinate tail. Recursive metric separation gives disjoint input blocks and disjoint finite-propagation outputs; an explicit blockwise rank-one projection proves the input copy is 1-complemented. Norm approximation transfers the lower bound to band-dominated maps, and compact/strict-singular ideal arguments give the distance and Bernstein consequences. Endpoint p=1 and c_0 issues were checked separately.

originality.rationale: Classical band-dominated Fredholm theory, limit-operator essential-norm formulas, metric limit-operator theory, and closed ideals of uniform Roe algebras are treated as prior art. Searches did not locate the exact classical-essential-norm formula via 1-complemented disjoint blocks, the resulting exact SS/FSS distances, or the Bernstein-number asymptotic for arbitrary locally finite metric spaces with nonuniform finite-dimensional fibers. Residual risk remains because the 2004 Rabinovich--Roch--Silbermann monograph and Roch's 2022 ideal paper were not exhaustively inspected theorem by theorem.

value.rationale: The result upgrades essential noncompactness to a sharp complemented-subspace witness, collapses three operator ideals within a broad finite-propagation closure, and identifies the asymptotic Bernstein scale without group, Property A, richness, Hilbert-space, or uniform-fiber-dimension assumptions.
